corrected_answer:
Assumptions: hold the model checkpoint, expert count, top-k, precision, software build, hardware and network topology, request mix, sequence-length distribution, concurrency, arrival rate, autoscaling, and warm-up constant; define tail latency at request level as p95/p99. Treat dropped or truncated tokens, failed requests, and retries as quality/goodput failures rather than latency improvements. For variant 26, the falsifiable hypothesis is: routing skew or expert-capacity overflow is the primary cause if a pre-specified routing or capacity policy, at matched offered load, reduces per-expert overflow/imbalance and p99 while preserving task quality and goodput. If those mechanisms improve without p99 improvement, the hypothesis is falsified for the dominant cause and queueing, batching, synchronization, all-to-all/network, placement, or compute contention should be investigated.

Measure per-expert token counts, router score/entropy and top-k assignments, capacity-factor limits, overflow, dropped and padded tokens, queue and expert-compute time, dispatch/combine and all-to-all latency, network congestion, placement/topology, batch composition, memory pressure, synchronization, retries, errors, and request outcomes. Stratify by prompt and sequence length, tenant/traffic slice, and concurrency. Separate workload-induced skew, router behavior, capacity limits, and implementation or placement defects.

Use a randomized fixed-seed replay on representative traffic, matched replicas, and a held-out workload; then run a canary at the same arrival rate. Compare the current policy with one pre-specified routing/load-balancing or capacity-factor change, changing one factor at a time and recording extra capacity/cost. Report p50/p95/p99, per-expert imbalance, overflow/drop/padding, queue/compute/all-to-all shares, throughput, goodput, task-quality scores, error/retry rates, SLO attainment, and cost with confidence intervals and slice regressions. Keep tuning data disjoint from evaluation.

Confounders include batch-size and sequence mix changes, cache/warm-up effects, network contention, kernel/compiler differences, autoscaling, retries, traffic drift, and topology changes.
